refero:593.summary: From an empty Templates library, the user names a new template, sets colors and fonts, edits it, and chooses to publish or keep as draft.
steps: Templates library with nothing listed yet
New template pop-up: name and two paths
Branded template: colors/fonts and Choose slides
Headline font list and Upload font
Template editor: 'You are editing a template'
steal: Before any templates exist, the screen explains why they help and offers 'Create' twice, at the top and in the middle (screen 1).
The new-template pop-up asks for a name first, then offers 'Build branded' or 'Customize from gallery' (screens 2-3).
Previews of each slide type (chart, sample, text) update live while you set brand colours and upload a font (screens 4-7).
A 'You are editing a template' banner stays visible, 'Publish this template?' offers Keep draft or Publish, and library cards then show a Draft label (screens 8-10).
avoid: A full presentation style builder (fonts, chart styles, slide layouts) is too much for the deliberately basic SCE editor, which should not become a Maestro-style tool.
refero:593.fit: Scenario manager: a strong pattern for scenarios in an organization library: start blank or from the gallery, keep drafts apart from published versions, and share on publish. It extends today's SCE editor without turning it into a slide product.

mobbin:f0c62f24-6d13-42f6-acb6-f36d7c2a8.summary: On a selected slide the user opens the Speaker notes side panel, types notes tied to that slide, then closes the panel (the notes icon keeps a presence indicator).
steps: Slide editor with Research Team selected
Speaker notes panel with empty placeholder
Speaker notes panel with text entered
Panel closed; notes icon with dot
steal: Notes for each slide sit in a side panel while the slide stays visible (screens 2-3).
The empty panel shows 'Add speaker notes…' until something is written (screen 2).
After the panel closes, a dot on the notes icon shows that notes exist (screen 4).
mobbin:f0c62f24-6d13-42f6-acb6-f36d7c2a8.fit: Scenario manager: a light pattern for SP or faculty scripts and cues in each scenario phase. It extends Briefing without a branching Maestro editor, and notes that only the presenter sees map to cue cards per role.
